title: Password on Sticky Note
description: A yellow adhesive sticky note stuck to the monitor bezel reading 'AdminPass2026!'.
explanation: Writing passwords on sticky notes completely bypasses authentication security. Anyone walking by can read or photograph your password.
remediation: Use a secure password manager or memorize a multi-word passphrase. Never write passwords in plain sight.

title: Unattended Unlocked Computer
description: The workstation is logged into an administrative account, but the user stepped away without locking the screen.
explanation: Leaving a device unlocked allows any passerby or bad actor to impersonate you, read confidential emails, or install rogue software in seconds.
remediation: Always lock your workstation before stepping away (Windows Key + L or Command + Control + Q).

title: Unidentified Rogue USB Drive
description: An unlabeled USB thumb drive found in the hallway is plugged directly into the front USB port.
explanation: Unknown USB drives can execute automated keystroke attacks (BadUSB) or deliver spyware/ransomware the moment they are inserted.
remediation: Never plug in unknown USB drives. Hand found drives to IT security or school staff for sandboxed inspection.

title: Postponed Security Update
description: A system tray notification: 'Critical security update postponed 42 days ago. System vulnerable.'
explanation: Software updates patch known security holes. Postponing updates leaves devices vulnerable to automated malware exploits.
remediation: Apply operating system and software patches promptly or enable automatic security updates.

title: Unencrypted HTTP Login
description: The browser address bar shows 'Not Secure' with an unencrypted http:// portal transmitting login credentials.
explanation: Plain HTTP transmits passwords in readable cleartext over the network, allowing eavesdroppers on the local network to intercept them.
remediation: Ensure websites use HTTPS (look for the secure lock icon) before entering any passwords or personal data.

title: Connected to Rogue Open Wi-Fi
description: The Wi-Fi tray shows connection to 'Free_Public_Internet_Unsecured' rather than the encrypted school network.
explanation: Open Wi-Fi networks without encryption allow attackers to execute Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks or host fake duplicate hotspots.
remediation: Use official password-protected WPA2/WPA3 networks and utilize a trusted VPN when on public Wi-Fi.

title: Sensitive Documents in Open Trash
description: Printed sheets with student account credentials and network diagram blueprints discarded into an open recycle bin.
explanation: Dumpster diving is a real-world reconnaissance technique where attackers search physical waste for sensitive credentials.
remediation: Sensitive records, student IDs, and credentials must always be shredded in a cross-cut shredder.

title: Uncovered Webcam Pointed at Desk
description: A high-resolution external webcam with no physical privacy shutter pointed directly at the keyboard and desk.
explanation: Spyware can silently activate webcams without warning indicator lights to spy on users or record keystrokes.
remediation: Use a sliding physical webcam cover or unplug external cameras when not in use.
